Hey Marie! I’ve actually read that when we have abortions bans, they decrease in states that have them but don’t necessarily decrease nationally because people just relocate to get their abortions. This study shows that in the 3 years after Roe v Wade was overturned, the total # of abortions nationally actually slightly increased.

I am also pro life morally and think that abortion is tragic, but I identify as pro choice legally. This is simply because studies have shown that bans are not the best way to decrease abortions overall. Better access to contraception, better sex education, better financial support and social support for women are things that actually show a drop. The Colorado Family Planning initiative is an amazing example. It increased access to birth control and saw a 50% drop in teen pregnancies and abortions.
